title: “My Foolish Heart” by Gordon Jenkins
text: "My Foolish Heart" is a popular song and jazz standard that was published in 1949. In the UK, the song reached number one on the chart based on sales of sheet music, staying at the top spot for 11 weeks in 1950.

title: “Rag Mop” by Ames Brothers
text: "Rag Mop" was a popular American song of the late 1940s–early 1950s. This 12-bar blues song, written by Tulsa western swing bandleader Johnnie Lee Wills and steel guitarist Deacon Anderson, was published in 1949.

title: “Bewitched” by Bill Snyder
text: "Bewitched" is a show tune and popular song from the 1940 Rodgers and Hart musical Pal Joey. It is part of the Great American Songbook.

title: “Hoop-Dee-Doo” by Perry Como & The Fontane Sisters with Mitchell Ayres
text: "Hoop-Dee-Doo" is a popular song published in 1950 with music by Milton Delugg and lyrics by Frank Loesser. The lyrics of this song are sometimes cited for their use of the phrase "soup and fish", meaning a man's formal dinner suit.

title: Austrian painter Arnulf Rainer founds the Hundsgruppe ("dog pack") with Arik Brauer, Ernst Fuchs and Josef Mikl.
text: Arnulf Rainer was an Austrian painter noted for his abstract informal art.

title: Paint by number kits introduced by Max S. Klein, an engineer and owner of the Palmer Paint Company of Detroit, and Dan Robbins.
text: Paint by number or painting by numbers kits are self-contained painting sets, designed to facilitate painting a pre-designed image. They generally include brushes, tubs of paint with numbered labels, and a canvas printed with borders and numbers.

title: Ernst Gombrich's The Story of Art is published by Phaidon Press.
text: Sir Ernst Hans Josef Gombrich was an Austro-Hungarian born art historian. After settling in England in 1936, he became a naturalised British citizen in 1947 and spent most of his working life in the United Kingdom.
